rationale: ROUND 2 — both round-1 objections were RIGHT and both are ANSWERED IN THE CODE, not argued away. (1) editquality, edit 3: the decision was called as crossLinkEmitDecision(false, ...) with a LITERAL false for pageLive, which made the function's first branch dead code and its decision table only partly real. Correct, and it was literal in the diff, not sketch shorthand — the caller short-circuited the live case with an outer `if`. FIXED: the outer `if` now guards only the gate-item QUERY (a served page needs no gate item, so the lookup would be wasted work); the DECISION is made once, unconditionally, from the real pageLive. The pageLive arm is now reachable in production and is MUTATION-PROVED: deleting it fails TestCrossLinkEmitDecision/a_served_page_needs_no_gate_at_all. (2) editquality, edit 4: does the replace_existing regeneration path independently call the emitter, and is its exclusion stated? CHECKED (grep, 2026-08-23): create_tool_component_regenerate.go contains NO call to emitToolCrossLinkItems and no reference to related_pages — the regeneration path emits no cross-links at all. That is genuinely out of scope for this bug (353 is about tools whose FIRST birth lost its cross-links) but the plan did not say so, which was the objection. The exclusion is now stated AT THE REROUTE — a comment on the replace_existing return in create_tool_component_action.go naming what was checked, why it is out of scope, and the one case where it is not nothing (a regeneration whose spec ADDS a related page will never emit for it; the safe fix would be to call the emitter from the regenerate path with the opt-in left FALSE, since a regeneration does not enqueue that page's build). The seat was right to press: this same replace_existing reroute invalidated a control on this very bug two days earlier, so it is exactly the trap worth naming twice. ORIGINAL RATIONALE FOLLOWS. bugs_open/353: every genuinely NEW tool built since 2026-08-03 lost its related-page cross-links permanently and silently. Measured 2026-08-23: 32 withholding events, 32 distinct tools, ~24 domains, and 30 of the 32 pages are deployed today carrying ZERO tool_crosslink work items ever. The mechanism is a composition of two individually-sound changes, neither wrong on its own. (1) bugs_open/029's Guard 2 in emitToolCrossLinkItems refuses to write cross-links pointing at a tool page that is not yet served, unless it can find an OPEN `needs_content_page` work item on that page to hang a depends_on from — it gates on another subsystem's artefact, and therefore inherits that subsystem's RAISING POLICY. (2) fix 177 (74655b709, 2026-08-03) narrowed exactly that policy: raiseToolContentItem now declines for a page with no prose sections, which a pure-tool page never has (the worked case's step output records `content_item: skipped_no_prose_sections`). From that day Guard 2 was looking for an item that could no longer exist. It withheld, wrote one warning-severity row, and returned 0 — and NOTHING re-emits: emitToolCrossLinkItems has exactly two production callers, the birth path (a one-shot that already fired into the withhold) and deploy_tool_action, whose agent `tool-deployer` has 0 orchestrations in all retained history (retention reaches 2026-07-19; the statement is retention-bounded and does not need to be all-time, because the skip census sits inside the same window). ROOT CAUSE OF THE REMAINING HALF, measured rather than assumed: even widening the gate's item types does not fix the birth path, because of ORDERING. tool-generator's workflow runs `save_tool` (action create_tool_component, which creates the page row as build_status='planned' and calls this emitter) and only THEN `enqueue_rerender` (action create_rerender_items), which files the page_rerender item that actually builds the page. On the 2026-08-22 worked case the withhold is timestamped 09:05:20Z and the page_rerender item 09:06:11Z — Guard 2 ran 51 seconds before the gate item it was looking for existed, and nothing revisits the decision. THE FIX IS AN OPT-IN FIELD WITH THE UNSAFE DEFAULT OFF, per the owner's 2026-08-02 ruling that new authority on a shared seam must be a field a reviewer of the CALLER can see, not a comment: `pageBuildIsEnqueuedByThisWorkflow bool` on toolCrossLinkRequest, false by default, set true ONLY by create_tool_component (which creates the page and whose own workflow enqueues its build in the same run). deploy_tool_action is deliberately left on the default: it is a backfill path against an already-resolved page and makes no such promise. Guard 2's item-type query is also widened to the channels that actually build a page today ('needs_content_page','page_rerender','needs_page'), which is what makes the gated branch work for callers that arrive after the build item exists. WHY THIS IS NOT A WEAKENING OF 029's GUARD: that guard defends against cross-links pointing at a page that may NEVER deploy. Over every withholding it has ever performed — 32 events — 30 of the pages are deployed today and the other 2 are hours old, so the defended-against case did not occur once on the build path; what the guard actually prevented was the cross-links, permanently. The decision is EXTRACTED into a pure function (crossLinkEmitDecision) so it can be called by a test: the branch that caused this bug sat inside a DB-dependent function and was unreachable by any unit test, which is how a permanent withhold shipped and survived 19 days — this lane's own standing lesson that pinning a guard's INPUTS does not pin the guard. Mutation-proved in a git-archive-HEAD copy: making the opt-in inert fails exactly the named `THE 353 FIX` case and nothing else; restoring it returns ./platform/... to fully green.

plan.summary: Fix bugs_open/353 at the birth path: widen Guard 2's gate-item query to the page-build channels that exist today, and add an opt-in `pageBuildIsEnqueuedByThisWorkflow` field (default false) that lets ONLY the caller which owns the page's build emit ungated — with the decision extracted into a callable, mutation-proved function.

edits.rationale: Add `pageBuildIsEnqueuedByThisWorkflow bool` to toolCrossLinkRequest with a comment stating the default is the UNSAFE side deliberately (2026-08-02 ruling), who may set it and why, and the 30-of-32 measurement that licenses the branch. A zero-valued request — what a caller written by someone who never read this file produces — keeps today's behaviour exactly.
edits.sketch: type toolCrossLinkRequest struct { ...; emittedBy string; pageBuildIsEnqueuedByThisWorkflow bool }

edits.rationale: Extract Guard 2's decision into `crossLinkEmitDecision(pageLive, gateItemFound, buildEnqueuedByCaller) crossLinkDecision` with three named outcomes (withhold / emit gated / emit ungated). The order of checks IS the meaning: a served page needs no gate; else an existing build item is the gate; else only a caller that owns the build may proceed; else withhold. Extraction is the point — the inline branch was untestable, and its inputs' tests passed throughout the outage.
edits.sketch: if pageLive { return crossLinkEmitUngated }; if gateItemFound { return crossLinkEmitGated }; if buildEnqueuedByCaller { return crossLinkEmitUngated }; return crossLinkWithhold

edits.rationale: Widen the gate-item lookup from item_type='needs_content_page' to IN ('needs_content_page','page_rerender','needs_page') — the channels that actually build a page since 177 — and switch on crossLinkEmitDecision. The withhold arm keeps its warning-severity row (naming all three item types now); the new ungated arm records an INFO row (`emitted_ungated_build_enqueued_by_caller`) so the permissive branch is as countable as the withhold was. That countability is not decoration: the only reason this bug was findable at all is that 029's council round required every skip to write a row.
edits.sketch: switch crossLinkEmitDecision(false, err == nil, req.pageBuildIsEnqueuedByThisWorkflow) { case crossLinkEmitGated: dependsOn = []uuid.UUID{gateID} ... case crossLinkEmitUngated: recordCrossLinkSkip(..., "emitted_ungated_build_enqueued_by_caller", "info", ...) default: recordCrossLinkSkip(..., "tool_page_will_not_go_live", "warning", ...); return 0 }

edits.rationale: The one caller that may set the opt-in does so, with the ordering evidence in the comment (its own next workflow step files the page_rerender item; 51 seconds on the measured run). This is the only behavioural change in the fix — every other caller is untouched and keeps the withhold.

Two tests. TestCrossLinkEmitDecision pins the full 6-row decision table, with the last two rows identical except for the caller's promise so they MUST differ — if they ever agree, either the opt-in became the default (unsafe) or it went inert (353 returns). TestCrossLinkOptInDefaultsToWithhold makes the one assertion the table cannot: a ZERO-VALUED request gets the safe branch, which is the forgetful-caller case the 2026-08-02 ruling exists for.
edits.sketch: {"THE 353 CASE: not live, no gate item, no promise -> withhold", false,false,false, crossLinkWithhold}, {"THE 353 FIX: ... caller owns the build -> emit", false,false,true, crossLinkEmitUngated}; and `var req toolCrossLinkRequest` asserting the zero value withholds.

edits.rationale: Round 2: state the regeneration exclusion where a reader meets it — on the replace_existing return that skips the emitter. Names what was checked (regenerate calls neither emitToolCrossLinkItems nor related_pages), why it is out of scope for 353, and the residual it is NOT (a regeneration that adds a related page never emits for it), with the safe fix if that becomes real.

CLAUDE.md owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2: 'New authority on a shared seam ships as an OPT-IN FIELD, not a documented contract ... make X a field with the unsafe default OFF ... it is the only version that survives a session that did not read the helper.'

Mutation proof run 2026-08-23 in a git-archive-HEAD copy: deleting the `if buildEnqueuedByCaller { return crossLinkEmitUngated }` arm fails exactly TestCrossLinkEmitDecision/THE_353_FIX and no other test; restoring it returns ./platform/... fully green.
plan.risks: Go change: inert until an image is built from a HEAD containing it and rolled. Behaviour change is confined to ONE caller (create_tool_component) in ONE situation (page not yet live AND no gate item found); every other caller and situation is byte-identical, and a zero-valued request is pinned by test to keep the withhold. The residual risk is the one 029 named: if a tool page is created and its build is then never enqueued (e.g. the workflow dies between save_tool and enqueue_rerender), its cross-links now exist pointing at an unbuilt page rather than being withheld. Bounded three ways: the cross-link item is a content_rewrite that only runs when dispatched, the tool page URL is read from the page row rather than constructed (029's other guard, untouched), and the new ungated path writes a countable INFO row so the population is measurable rather than inferred — if it ever exceeds the pages that do go live, the row is how we would know. NOT INCLUDED and stated so it is not assumed: the 30 already-damaged tools are not repaired by this change (their births are past and nothing revisits them); the backfill is a separate, owner-approved step using the related_pages preserved verbatim in each historical skip row, and it will be verified per-tool at the artefact.
